hyperedges.label: Design Principles the Team Agreed On
Agentic Gatherings Coordination Flow (profile, time check, preference check, approval, booking verification)

nodes.label: Idea: Butler Shopping Agent
nodes.rationale: Kept as host mode and as the checkout pattern. Needs a credential store for Instacart, Costco, Walmart, Temu.

nodes.label: Host Mode
nodes.rationale: This is where the shopping task and Stripe checkout reconnect to the hackathon challenge.

nodes.label: Idea: Lifestyle Food Agent
nodes.rationale: Scoped down to food and dietary restriction; feeds host mode.

nodes.label: Amplitude + Statsig (agent analytics, flags, experimentation)
nodes.rationale: Amplitude was called 'a little hard' by the team.

nodes.label: Challenge: Shopping Agent With an Audit Trail
nodes.norm_label: challenge: shopping agent with an audit trail
nodes.rationale: Team reading: shopping is a nice-to-have, not mandatory. The audit trail is the part worth keeping whatever we build.

nodes.label: Submission Requirements (repo, demo video, tools, team)
nodes.norm_label: submission requirements (repo, demo video, tools, team)
nodes.rationale: Settles the team debate: a demo video and repo are required, a live link is optional.

nodes.label: Superlinked (task-specific inference, SIE Serverless)
nodes.rationale: Called 'cool but inference is different' by the team.

nodes.label: Theme: Personal Agent Beyond a Chat Window
nodes.norm_label: theme: personal agent beyond a chat window

nodes.label: Principle: Output Is an Action, Not a Chat Reply
nodes.norm_label: principle: output is an action, not a chat reply
nodes.rationale: Stated target: input is your profile, output is a Stripe checkout.

nodes.label: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
nodes.rationale: The team uses the ADK concepts for product design and build orchestration but is not required to use ADK itself.

nodes.label: Agentic AI Builder Lab with Google Cloud (AI Camp SF, 2026-11-19)
nodes.norm_label: agentic ai builder lab with google cloud (ai camp sf, 2026-11-19)

nodes.label: Annie Wong (Developer Relations Engineer, Google Cloud)
nodes.norm_label: annie wong (developer relations engineer, google cloud)

nodes.label: Graph Workflow (nodes and edges)
nodes.rationale: More reliable than a pure multi-agent system because the order of work is fixed by the graph instead of decided by agents at runtime. Start small with a single agent and tools, then move the process into a graph.

nodes.label: Idea: Price Comparison
nodes.rationale: Rejected as too generic and trend dependent.

nodes.label: Principle: Be Specific (not a generic do-anything agent)
nodes.norm_label: principle: be specific (not a generic do-anything agent)
nodes.rationale: A generic do-anything agent is just Muse with a front end; Muse already handles browser, apps and Gmail.

nodes.label: Idea: Caregiver Agent
nodes.rationale: Rejected: touches medical advice.

nodes.label: Idea: Clothing and Sizing Agent
nodes.rationale: Rejected: sizes, styles and fittings are too hard.

nodes.label: Principle: Use Domain Data Others Do Not Have
nodes.norm_label: principle: use domain data others do not have
nodes.rationale: For food the differentiator would be fresh ingredient data from restaurants or food producers.

nodes.label: Idea: Out-of-Stock Substitution
nodes.rationale: Rejected: DoorDash and restaurants already do this.

nodes.label: Railway (backend and long-running agents)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for backend and long-running agents because a teammate has a paid plan; Vercel is front end only.

nodes.label: Human Gate (request-input node)
nodes.rationale: Use for content direction choices, payment approvals and sensitive database actions; the workflow suspends indefinitely until the human responds.

nodes.label: Long-Running Tool
nodes.rationale: In production use a cron job, scheduler or watcher instead of a polling loop.

nodes.label: Persistent Database
nodes.rationale: Required to keep state across server crashes and long waits.

nodes.label: Principle: Human Only Says Yes or No
nodes.norm_label: principle: human only says yes or no

nodes.label: Principle: Keep Working With the Laptop Lid Closed
nodes.norm_label: principle: keep working with the laptop lid closed
nodes.rationale: The agent runs in the cloud with continuous memory; the theme asks for more than a chat box.

nodes.label: Idea: Dietary Label Reader
nodes.rationale: Folded into the profile. Criticized: identifying allergens is something agents can already do.

nodes.label: Personal Agent Profile (calendar, dietary restrictions, allergens, cuisine, age)
nodes.norm_label: personal agent profile (calendar, dietary restrictions, allergens, cuisine, age)

nodes.label: Long-Term Memory (memory service)
nodes.rationale: Memory read runs in a before-model callback so preferences load before the agent reasons; memory write runs in an after-agent callback saving a session summary. Facts are consolidated and deduplicated, not duplicated.

nodes.label: Principle: Learn From Feedback
nodes.rationale: Yes/no answers and post-purchase reviews update the profile so bad recommendations are not repeated.

nodes.label: Agentic Gatherings (group dinner and party agent)
nodes.norm_label: agentic gatherings (group dinner and party agent)
nodes.rationale: Converged direction, proposed for team agreement. Today one organizer has to ask every person for availability and food preference, which takes time.

nodes.label: Open Questions (mode, demo action, data sharing, sponsors, owners, Senso eligibility)
nodes.norm_label: open questions (mode, demo action, data sharing, sponsors, owners, senso eligibility)

nodes.label: Idea: Party and Event Agent
nodes.rationale: Merged into party mode.

nodes.label: Agent-to-Agent Privacy Concern
nodes.rationale: One teammate called agent-to-agent communication sketchy; privacy of shared data is the worry. Answer given: each person owns their own agent and one agent coordinates.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph (shared memory)
nodes.rationale: Shared memory in the repo so nobody's agent re-reads raw context.

nodes.label: Vi (owns the AI brain: memory, knowledge graph, inference, connecting agents)
nodes.norm_label: vi (owns the ai brain: memory, knowledge graph, inference, connecting agents)

nodes.label: Sponsor Selection Guidance (pick two or three)
nodes.norm_label: sponsor selection guidance (pick two or three)
nodes.rationale: Pick two or three sponsors that fit the storyline; do not use all of them.

nodes.label: Judging (no published criteria)
nodes.rationale: The 'three sponsor products minimum' mentioned in the brainstorm is unverified; confirm with organizers.

nodes.label: Form Factor: Web App Favored
nodes.rationale: Debate was iOS app versus web app versus phone call; web app favored, an iOS app is not needed.

nodes.label: Google Calendar
nodes.rationale: Preferred over Apple Calendar because it has an MCP server.

nodes.label: Persona (detect agents, verify people; age and identity verification)
nodes.norm_label: persona (detect agents, verify people; age and identity verification)

nodes.label: Function Node
nodes.rationale: Use a function node (deterministic code) whenever the step does not need judgment.

nodes.label: Audit Trail (recorded path through the graph)
nodes.norm_label: audit trail (recorded path through the graph)

nodes.label: Principle: Show the Work
nodes.rationale: Users do not trust AI to click buy unless they can verify why a product was chosen; visualize what the agent does in the backend. Matches the audit trail in the challenge.

nodes.label: Audit Trail (context and steps behind each action)
nodes.norm_label: audit trail (context and steps behind each action)

nodes.label: Idea: Accessibility Agent
nodes.rationale: Parked. Local store inventory and transit range were noted as accessibility factors.

nodes.label: Idea: Voice-Only Personal Agent
nodes.rationale: Parked: called a headache to implement.
